newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-WORLD TOP TWO SAMPRAS AND CHANG CRASH OUT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-WORLD TOP TWO SAMPRAS AND CHANG CRASH OUT.

text.p: The world's two top players Pete Sampras and Michael Chang crashed out of the Italian Open on Tuesday with the crowd whistling and jeering as the Americans lost.
Top seed Sampras, beaten at the same stage on his last visit in 1995, was booed on his way to a 7-6 6-4 defeat at the hands of unseeded compatriot and friend Jim Courier.

It was his second successive defeat on clay after losing to Sweden's Magnus Larsson at Monte Carlo last month and the first time since 1995 that he has gone out in the first round of two tournaments in succession.
Second seed Chang's 6-3 6-2 loss to Argentine Hernan Gumy was also his second consecutive first round elimination following defeat at the American red clay court championships.
It was the first time the Italian Open had lost its top two seeds in the first round.
Sampras said he knew he was in for a tough match as soon as he drew Courier, who took him to five sets in Paris last year.
"It was a tough draw for both of us. We know each other's games," he said. "But you've got to play the cards you are drawn and he came out fractionally ahead of me."
Both players traded breaks in their opening service games before the remainder of the set went with serve and into a tiebreak.
The world number one lost his serve in the very opening match of the second as Courier raced into a 3-1 lead.
At 30-40 in the fifth, Sampras served a double fault provoking a chorus of whistles from the crowd.
"It's very tough to play if you're not playing well here," said the American afterwards. "When they're hissing and whatever, it makes it harder. It's not fun."
"I guess that if you're not playing well, they think you're not trying. But I was fighting out there."
With Courier serving for the set at 5-3, Sampras silenced the crowd by gaining one break back, but two games later a driving forehand into the corner from Courier ended it.
"It's a good day for me. I've beaten the world number one and that doesn't happen very often to me now," said Courier, a former world number one himself and twice champion in Rome.
Apart from Chang, the unseeded Gumy's only other victory over a top 10 player was Courier in Rome last year.

Chang, whose game was riddled with errors, showed sparkle only in the first game of the second set when he broke Gumy. The Argentine number one proceeded to break the former French Open champion's serve three times.
Serving at 0-30 1-4 in the second, Chang responded to a slow handclap by an increasingly frustrated centre court crowd with an ace and net cord to hold serve.
It was his last sign of resistance.
The last point of the match summed up Chang's day. Faced with an easy kill at the net, the American let the ball pass thinking it was going deep. He was wrong.
"It wasn't the best match of my career but it was probably the best win," said Gumy.
Chang, who had dominated the hard court season, said he had problems with the transition from hardcourt to clay.
"I don't feel as if I've made that transition yet."
Boris Becker, who lost to Sampras in the 1994 final on his last appearance at the Foro Italico, returned to Rome with a 7-6 6-2 win over local favourite Andrea Gaudenzi.
But Andrei Medvedev, unbeatable in the German Open last week, made a swift exit to Australia's Scott Draper.
Britain's Tim Henman staved off three matchpoints and then won after opponent Roberto Carretero of Spain retired in the final set with a leg injury.
"I was a little bit surprised that at 2-0 he was standing at the net with his hand up, so I was pretty quick to shake it," said Henman, returning from two-months out due to injury.
